sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2017. Lolo-Burmese lexical database (xlsx). Zenodo 1249173.
sources.note: No Nisi doculect; the only Wenshan/Yanshan columns are Azha, Zuoke and Polo (from YYFC 1983 / Lama). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2014. Mondzish: a new subgroup of Lolo-Burmese. 20 pp. Zenodo 1127814.
sources.note: Nothing about Nisi; the paper covers the 'Lolo'-named groups of Wenshan (Maang, Mantsi, Mango, etc., i.e. much of the population Operation China called Southeastern Luoluopo) but never mentions Nisi/yso. Checked for identity only.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2013. New endangered Tibeto-Burman languages of southwestern China: Mondzish, Longjia, Pherbu, and others. 24 pp. Zenodo 1127796.
sources.note: No mention of Nisi/yso at all.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority / Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Change Request Number 2007-083: [yso] 'Yi, Southeastern Lolo' renamed 'Nisi' (adopted 2008-01-14). SIL International. 8 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Name-change rationale only ('Nisi' closer to the autonym, attested in Wenshan xian zhi 1999 and fieldwork; one Nisi speaker interviewed in 2005); no linguistic data of any kind.

Web page, yixueyanjiu.com details.jsp?class=3&id=568.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: General Yi statement only: '4. 一般有3至4个声调,调比较简单。多平调和降调,没有曲折调。少数方言如东南部方言弥勒、西部方言的姚安各有个五个调的现象。云、贵二省境内少数彝语方言点存在的低升调(13),多用作语法手段或拼写汉语新借词。' and '甚至文西土语内部通话也有很大的困难'. Nothing on stress; nothing specific to Nisi — not counted as a statement for this languoid.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record nisi1238 (classification Unclassified Southeastern Ngwi; Glottolog's most extensive description = Honghe Yi Zu Cidian 2002, tagged dictionary; 0 grammar/sketch/phonology refs).
sources.note: Nothing; bibliographic record only. Confirms no descriptive reference is known to Glottolog.

sources.citation: Hattaway, Paul. 2000. Operation China: introducing all the peoples of China. Carlisle: Piquant. Profile 'Luoluopo, Southeastern', p. 315 (Asia Harvest online reprint).
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnographic profile: pop. 35,800 (1999, J. Pelkey), Maguan/Funing/Xichou/Malipo/Honghe counties, 'speaks a language belonging to the Southeastern group of Yi languages'; dialects Han/Hua/Bai/Hei Lolo. This is the entity Ethnologue 15 coded [yso].

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Nisi language (China)' [redirects to 'Nisoish languages'], 'Southeastern Loloish languages', 'Loloish languages', 'Wenshan Zhuang and Miao Autonomous Prefecture' (Yi subgroups from the 2000/2005 prefecture gazetteers); Wikipedia (zh) 东南彝语. Wikitext dumps.
sources.note: Nothing. en 'Southeastern Loloish languages' states yso 'Nisi (China)', previously 'Southeastern Lolo Yi', is 'still unclassified within branches of Southeastern Loloish'; 'Loloish languages' table gives yso pop. 36,000. No linguistic data anywhere.

sources.citation: Wang Chengyou 王成有. 2003. Yiyu fangyan bijiao yanjiu 彝语方言比较研究 [Comparative study of Yi dialects]. Chengdu: Sichuan Minzu Chubanshe. ISBN 7-5409-2765-8.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Gives phonological inventories (initials/finals/tones) for ~44 Yi datapoints incl. Wenshan; if any datapoint corresponds to the Nisi/'Lolo' Yi of Wenshan-Xichou-Malipo it would be the only phonology in print. Coverage of Nisi unverified.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. Dialectology as Dialectic: Interpreting Phula Variation (Trends in Linguistics 229). Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. doi:10.1515/9783110245851
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL3311.Y5 P45 2011) (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL3311.Y5 P45 2011
sources.note: Pelkey is the person who renamed [yso] and surveyed the area in 2005; the monograph's Southeastern Ngwi overview (pp. 368-371, 431ff) may say what Nisi is and whether any data exist. Will not contain a Nisi stress rule but would settle identity.
